title: Effective practice within day service centres for people with intellectual disabilities: a systematic review of quantitative research
content:
by James Belsey, Rachel Harrison

Background

This review aimed to identify areas of consensus, contention, and any gaps in the literature that may exist with regard to what constitutes best practice and effective provision for people with intellectual disabilities within day service centres.

Materials and Methods

The review was prospectively registered on the PROSPERO registry (ID: CRD42024585737) and conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines. The International Bibliography of the Social Sciences, Scopus, and PsycInfo databases were searched in April 2026 for peer-reviewed research that investigated the effectiveness of day service provision in non-residential settings. Methodological quality was assessed using the Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomised studies and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal tools for non-randomised studies of different designs. Results were synthesised according to the Grades of Recommendation, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework.

Results

16 studies were included and methodological weaknesses were commonly found. The results showed that challenging behaviours were effectively reduced through positive interactions between staff members and people with intellectual disabilities. Furthermore, exercise-based interventions were successfully employed within day service centres, leading to positive changes in several health and fitness parameters. Trends in the data were generally in favour of community-oriented day service settings for activity engagement and participation.

Conclusions

Day service centres offer significant opportunities for enhancing communication, engagement, relationships, health and community integration for people with intellectual disabilities. However, the current evidence base is marked by considerable variability in methodological quality and the certainty in the resultant findings.
